The source does not state that the first table row is the same test or time point as the narrative values, so they are kept as separate measurements and not treated as a conflict or merged. Tables 2 and 3 first rows equal the narrative coagulation and bilirubin values but are likewise not merged. The discussion compares current coagulation with "levels at admission (Table 2)", but no table row is labelled as the admission test, so the first rows are not given an admission time.
The source does not define the "R" column of Table 1 or give dates or days for the numbered table rows; Table 2 has no 4th row. Row ordinals are kept literally and no calendar time is derived.

The case text reports normal liver function at the annual physical exam, while the discussion attributes elevated bilirubin to pre-existing impaired liver function associated with hepatitis B. Both are recorded as stated; no reconciliation is inferred.

The discussion says the ALT and ALP levels point to both hepatocellular and cholestatic damage, while another sentence says the patient presented with a hepatocellular pattern and later transitioned to a cholestatic pattern. Only the explicitly stated patterns and the stated transition are recorded as facts.
Causality is classified "probable" by RUCAM and Naranjo, so drug-induced liver injury is recorded as provisional although the title and abstract call the injury minocycline-induced.

The patient blood type was Rh-negative, which complicated plasma matching for plasmapheresis, and DPMAS with renal replacement therapy was employed. The source does not state that plasmapheresis was planned or performed, so no plasmapheresis fact is recorded. The abstract names artificial liver therapy with CRRT, which may be the same as DPMAS with RRT but is not stated as such.
The uric acid value is printed as 187 mmol/L in the source; the unit is recorded as printed. Table 2 header APTT_rati is printed truncated.

Reported times for symptom onset: the abstract says fatigue, jaundice, abdominal bloating and discomfort occurred after 1 week, while the case text lists the presenting complaints and the minocycline start 1 week prior; no presentation date or day count is given.

The case text says she "presented" and later counts DPMAS days "after admission"; it never says the presentation and the admission are the same event. A separate admission event is kept; the presentation is ordered before in-hospital DPMAS only as the presentation opening the stay. The abstract's artificial liver therapy with CRRT may be the DPMAS with RRT of the case text but is not identified as such, so the two stay separate events.
